title: Mahershala Ali Confirms Marvel's Blade Is Dead After Seven Years in Limbo
excerpt: The two-time Oscar winner told GQ he has moved on from the vampire-hunter film, while Marvel's Kevin Feige admitted the studio feels like a gigantic loser for failing to deliver.
body:
• Mahershala Ali confirmed in a GQ interview that he has moved on from Marvel's Blade, the vampire-hunter film first announced in 2019 that was never produced
  • Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige admitted the studio felt like a gigantic loser for failing to deliver the project, which went through multiple directors and rewrites
  • Ali is now reuniting with former Blade director Bassam Tariq on an original film titled Your Mother, Your Mother, Your Mother
  • The cancellation marks one of the most high-profile failures in the Marvel Cinematic Universe's history

Seven Years of False Starts

https://youtube.com/watch?v=pasVjJ2nxLg

Mahershala Ali has closed the book on Blade. In a wide-ranging GQ interview published Thursday, the two-time Academy Award winner confirmed he has moved on from Marvels long-troubled vampire-hunter film, bringing a definitive end to one of the most protracted development failures in superhero cinema history.

We feel like a gigantic loser that we were unable to make that movie.

Kevin Feige, Marvel Studios President

Ali was announced as the new Blade at San Diego Comic-Con in July 2019, stepping into a role made iconic by Wesley Snipes across three films between 1998 and 2004. The casting was met with widespread enthusiasm. Ali, coming off Oscar wins for Moonlight and Green Book, brought both prestige and genuine excitement to a character Marvel hoped would anchor a new corner of the MCU.

A Revolving Door of Directors

What followed was anything but smooth. Bassam Tariq, the Pakistani American director of the critically acclaimed Mughal Mowgli, was hired to direct in 2022 but departed that September, citing creative differences. Yann Demange, known for 71 and the HBO series Lovecraft Country, replaced him but also exited the project. By the time a third director was being sought, the film had cycled through at least five screenwriters, and its release date had been pushed back repeatedly from November 2023 to September 2024 to November 2025, and then off the schedule entirely.

https://x.com/comicbookaddt/status/2083328428963737914

Kevin Feiges candid admission of failure is striking for a studio that has grossed over $30 billion at the worldwide box office. In the same GQ piece, Feige acknowledged that Marvel simply could not crack the project, despite Alis sustained commitment and patience.

Moving On With Tariq

The most telling detail in Alis departure may be where hes heading next. The actor is reuniting with Bassam Tariq on an original film titled Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. The project, which Tariq is writing and directing, suggests both artists have found what they were looking for outside the Marvel machine.

For Ali, the experience does not appear to have soured him on ambitious projects. He remains one of the most sought-after actors in Hollywood, with recent roles in Swan Song and the Apple TV+ series Disclaimer alongside Cate Blanchett earning strong reviews. But the Blade saga will inevitably be remembered as a cautionary tale about the limits of franchise filmmaking, even for a studio that once seemed incapable of misfiring.

What It Means for Marvel

Blades cancellation adds to a growing list of post-Endgame struggles for Marvel Studios. The studio has faced criticism for oversaturation, declining box-office returns for several Phase Five and Six releases, and a perception that its quality control has slipped. Feiges willingness to publicly label the studio a loser on a specific project marks a notable shift in tone from a company that has historically projected relentless optimism about its slate.

Whether Marvel will attempt to reboot Blade with a different actor remains unclear. For now, the dhampir vampire hunter returns to limbo and Ali moves on to projects where the scripts actually get finished.
